text: That's why I'd tell everyone not to dance on MDMA at all, however good the music is, since dancing makes the heat and the sweat that drain their salt. And really, what's the point of MDMA if someone wants to dance? For that they can take some San Pedro cactus or mescaline, which is way way safer, and still very therapeutic. Real MDMA, the kind that's therapeutic and helps people access very early childhood trauma, possibly better than San Pedro can in some cases, isn't the kind people want to dance on, which is why you don't see people in the MAPS trials of MDMA therapy saying "I NEED TO DANCE!" No, they're sitting there doing the therapy, and even if the science isn't clear on this yet, I and everyone I know are totally clear about what the real thing feels like. It's not like "I don't feel like dancing", it's like "I can barely move", couch lock. So if a pill makes someone feel like dancing, I'm highly suspicious that it contains amphetamines, or that it isn't real MDMA at all, maybe 6-APB, a similar drug. That might also be why women get low sodium far more often than men outside the lab, where what people take as "MDMA" is ecstasy, while a [lab study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4923534/) that gave people pure MDMA and water found no difference between them. The lab also dosed everyone by their weight, though, so it couldn't show how much harder the same pill hits a smaller body.
reader: someone about to go to a festival with friends who plan to take MDMA and dance all night, reading this the day before
